The paper was published in IEEE Journal of Oceanic Engineering, Vol. OE-12, No. 2, April 1987.
Radar cross section reduction is achieved by multiple passive impedance loadings on conducting thin-wire scatterers.
The method of moments is used to solve for induced currents on the scatterer.
Biquadratic programming is applied as an iterative optimization method to find optimal passive impedances.
Single impedance loading becomes less effective as the wire length increases.
Loads must be placed where the induced current is non-zero for effective scattering control.
For a straight wire, loads spaced every 0.5 to 0.7 wavelengths are needed for near-zero RCS.
A circular loop scatterer showed near-zero backscattering cross section with one to three loads for loop lengths up to about 3 wavelengths.
For longer loops (~5 wavelengths), more loads are necessary to achieve significant RCS reduction.
Experimental measurements for a circular loop with two loads agreed well with numerical results.
A rectangular wire frame with nine loads (six independently adjusted) reduced RCS from 10.6 λ² to 0.08 λ² after 12 iterations.
Passive loads have non-negative resistance (R_L ≥ 0) ensuring energy dissipation or storage without amplification.
The bistatic radar cross section is calculated from the far-field scattered electric field component.
The iterative biquadratic programming method updates one load impedance at a time, analytically minimizing RCS at each step.
The radar cross section decreases monotonically during the iterative optimization process.
The method can be applied to arbitrarily shaped thin-wire scatterers.
Radar echo enhancement can be treated similarly by the developed formulation.
The method of moments reduces integral equations to a system of linear equations for unknown currents.
The paper includes numerical examples for straight wires, circular loops, and rectangular wire frames.
Load placement is critical; placing loads at current nulls is ineffective for RCS reduction.
